newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake Energy says completes well.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake Energy says completes well.

text.p: Chesapeake Energy Corp said it completed the reentry of the Lyles 31#1 well.

The well tested at a daily rate of 2,300 barrels of oil and 11.6 million cubic feet of natural gas per day on a 30/64-inch choke with flowing tubing pressure of 5,400 psi from a new lateral, Chesapeake said.
The well had earlier been abandoned due to excessive water production from its initial lateral, the company said.

"The success of this well is attributable to the interpretation of newly acquired seismic information and the learning curve benefits from Chesapeake's drilling activities during the past year in the Louisiana Trend," it said.
Chesapeake owns about 25,000 acres in the area surrounding the Lyles and a 98 percent working interest in the well.

The company said it plans to begin drilling three additional wells in the area in the next several months. Chesapeake said it expects the Lyle well to begin producing early in the fourth fiscal quarter after production facilities have been completed.
In the St. Landry portion of the Louisiana Trend, Chesapeake said it completed what it believes is the world's deepest horizontal well, the Grezaffi 191.
The well tested at a daily rate of 3,200 barrels of oil and 4.1 million cubic feet of natural gas on a 24/64-inch choke with flowing tubing pressure of 3,600 psi.
Chesapeake owns about 150,000 acres in the St. Landry area and a 98 percent working interest in the Grezaffi well.

The company plans to begin drilling two more wells in the area in the next several months. "Chesapeake expects this well to begin producing late in the third quarter of fiscal 1997 after production facilities have been completed," it said.
Chesapeake is an independent energy producer.
